purpose: Separate same-code execution-condition variation from the cached-Q8 candidate effect. Never normalize latency by counters and call the normalized number a measured speedup.
pilot: Same frozen CLIs, Q8 Llama-3.2-3B, four workers, prefix cache off, ABBA server sequence. One warmup and three measured32-token requests per server. This shorter diagnostic workload is not the previous64-token protocol and cannot independently authorize adoption.

screening_thresholds_declared_before_pil.gc_and_io: Retain all samples. Report GC cycle/pause, page-in and disk-read changes; do not silently discard or post-select clean samples. Different GC/I/O activity prevents a simple attribution to kernel code.

interpretation: These thresholds are operational screens, not statistical equivalence bounds or proof of a causal effect. Failure means the complete batch is ineligible for an adoption timing claim; individual samples remain diagnostic evidence.
bounded_followup_declared_before_executi: If the first pilot shows a time-rate drift, allow exactly one extended-warmup pilot: eight warmups and three measured32-token requests per ABBA leg. Same thresholds, no sample selection and no timing normalization. Preserve the first pilot separately. If drift remains, stop timing-based adoption work rather than endlessly repeating until a favorable batch appears.
adoption_gate: Only after a stable pilot: a separately identified64-token confirmation with same-code controls and at least three independent before/after blocks, plus FP32/Q4 and prefill checks for the larger shared descriptor. Require exact outputs/token IDs, lifecycle/race/compatibility checks and no reproducible material regression. Any3% non-regression screen is operational, not a statistical guarantee. Full source/receipt review before production application; no commit, push or merge implied.
counter_method: Nonprivileged proc_pid_rusage RUSAGE_INFO_V6, own benchmark processes only. Official local SDK struct used by compiled C helper. CPU time fields are Mach ticks, converted using mach_timebase_info, and independently calibrated against a controlled Python child's process_time_ns. Preserve raw counters. P-only fields follow XNU performance-CPU accounting, not a thread-affinity guarantee. cycles_per_cpu_ns is an aggregate proxy, not a direct core-frequency measurement.
